## 1. Sri Lanka and the IMF reached a staff-level agreement on the seventh review of the four-year Extended Fund Facility.

The accord would release <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">SDR 254 million</span> (an IMF reserve asset called Special Drawing Rights) worth about $345m, lifting total disbursements under the programme to roughly <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$2.7bn</span>, once the Fund’s Board signs off. Board consideration hinges on the presentation to Parliament of the 2027 Budget in line with programme parameters and on a financing assurances review confirming multilateral contributions and sufficient progress with debt restructuring.

Economic activity expanded by <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">4.2% in 2026Q2</span>, marking an eleventh straight quarter of growth, while gross official reserves reached $6.9 billion at end‑August. The Fund warned that the Middle East war and El Niño (a climate pattern that disrupts rainfall and temperatures) could rekindle inflation and strain the balance of payments, and said monetary policy must be ready to tighten if second‑round price effects strengthen.

## 2. The President announced plans to amend contracts with private fuel suppliers after queues and curtailed deliveries.

The head of state said the CPC (Ceylon Petroleum Corporation, the state oil company) had lifted its diesel share from 58% to 77% as private operators cut volumes, and warned of legal action if supply limits persisted. Two companies had sought diesel increases of <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 132 per litre</span> and Rs. 116 per litre, but the Government capped the adjustment to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">around Rs. 10 per litre</span> and absorbed a Rs. 70 subsidy to protect consumers.

Operators await <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">written communication with a ceiling</span> before setting their own rates and account for about 35 percent of supply, while the ministry maintains that private players are free to price. Officials said revised agreements would give the state greater flexibility to act when retail networks falter and to prioritise consumer interests over commercial preferences.

## 3. The Government’s anti-corruption drive saw the arrest of former First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa over alleged misuse of funds.

Investigators from the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption</span> detained her and a former bank chairman in a probe into <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 10 million</span> transferred from a state bank to a charity for a CT scanner that was not supplied. A court remanded her until October 13 and separately dismissed an anticipatory bail petition on jurisdictional grounds.

Parliament meanwhile passed the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill</span> without a vote to streamline investigations, fix drafting discrepancies and move asset and liability declarations to a centralised electronic system. In a parallel rights case, the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka</span> ordered Customs to release two detained Tamil-language books, ruling the seizure violated freedom of expression and equality guarantees.

## 4. The Government tabled the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill to replace the 1979 PTA.

The draft permits the police, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">armed forces and Coast Guard</span> to stop, search and arrest on reasonable suspicion and allows <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">detention up to one year</span> through Defence Secretary orders, subject to magistrate visits and medical referrals. An <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">independent review committee</span> appointed by the minister would examine necessity, legality and proportionality, while rights groups flagged overbroad definitions that could chill protest and speech.

Separately, the Court of Appeal issued <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">writs of mandamus</span> directing the railway and wildlife authorities to regulate speeds, upgrade training and prepare habitat plans to curb elephant deaths from train collisions, and fixed a three‑month progress review. Judges said the framework for infrastructure should include practical safeguards for wildlife alongside operational discipline.

## 5. The Cabinet presented the Appropriation for 2027 to Parliament.

Total expenditure is projected at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 4,992 billion</span>, up from Rs. 4,545 billion in 2026, with health at Rs. 590 billion, education at Rs. 328 billion and defence at Rs. 458 billion. The second reading of the Budget speech was scheduled for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Nov. 12, 2026</span>.

## 6. The World Bank said output returned to 2018 levels but household recovery remained uneven.

The lender noted <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">12 consecutive quarters</span> of expansion and 4.7% growth in the first half of 2026, but estimated poverty at 16.9% in 2025 with wages still below pre‑crisis levels. It urged a shift from state-led demand to private investment and exports, highlighting the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">agrifood system</span> as a one‑sixth share of GDP with scope for reform in trade, quality infrastructure and finance.

## 7. Inflation in September stayed at 8% on the Colombo Consumer Price Index.

The national index read 8.1% in August, while real GDP grew 4.2% in the second quarter and the rupee eased to around <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 330.98/USD</span> on 9 October. In the bond market, the 2034s last traded near <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">12.10%</span> with the curve largely steady on subdued volumes.

## 8. The Government moved to revise prison rules for Buddhist monks produced in court.

A committee was asked to propose amendments within <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">two weeks</span> to the standing orders under the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Prisons Ordinance of 1877</span> so that imprisoned clergy may, on the recommendation of the relevant Nikaya, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">wear their robes</span> when escorted outside. Officials said current regulations lack specific provisions for monks and that changes would follow consultation with the Maha Sangha.

## 9. The national carrier suspended flights to Riyadh until October 18 after security incidents at the airport.

Services were paused following a reported attack that damaged facilities, with the airline stating operations would resume when conditions are suitable for commercial flights. Passengers were advised to use the 1979 hotline or the website for rebooking and refunds.

## 10. Three private fuel operators sought formal permission to set pump prices under a maximum ceiling.

<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Lanka Indian Oil Company, RM Parks and Sinopec</span>, together responsible for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">35 percent of supply</span>, told officials they could adjust rates once they received <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">written communication from the Ministry</span> setting a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">maximum ceiling</span> for each product. The Energy Ministry reiterated that non‑state players are free to set prices but said legal clarity would avoid disputes over supply obligations.
